Subject: 5 stars for Arroyo Precision Works — adapter plate and baffle for our near-IR camera

Arroyo Precision Works gets 5 stars from us. I am writing this out in detail because other labs and our purchasing staff read these pages, and because the specific reasons these people are good are worth more than a generic endorsement.

What we needed: a camera-to-dewar adapter plate and a light baffle tube for our near-IR camera, both 6061-T6, black anodized, with internal threads on the baffle. The parts had to be right for a Palomar run on the 200-inch on the night of November 18, so there was not a lot of slack in the schedule.

Turnaround: our large national vendor quoted us six weeks. Arroyo quoted 21 days and had finished parts on site nine days after the PO. They did bill a rush setup fee, and they still beat their own quoted lead time by more than a week, so even including that fee the value was well worth it. The quote itself came back the next morning, which was more than I expected.

They actually read the drawing, and that is the part I want to be honest about, because the error was mine. I sent them a drawing where the bolt circle on sheet 2 was dimensioned "4.125" while every other dimension on that sheet was in millimeters — the correct value is 104.8 mm (4.125 in), and I had copied the number from an old drawing for a previous camera. If they had simply cut it, the screws would have landed inside the bore and we would have found out at the telescope, with two weeks to fix it. Instead they stopped, flagged it, and asked me to confirm before cutting anything. That is exactly the behavior you want from a shop that is about to hold a tolerance on a near-IR instrument, and it is worth much more to me than a small price difference.

Delivery: Ruben brought the parts to the Robinson Lab himself on his way to another supplier in Glendale, and did not charge us for the delivery. Small thing, but it is the kind of thing that tells you how they run their shop.

Fit test on Monday, November 9: all eight screws went in with no forcing, flatness across the plate face measured under 0.01 mm on a dial indicator, the baffle threads were smooth, a 300 s dark frame with the lab lights on showed no light leak, and the anodizing was even with no bare spots. Everything works, and the parts go to Palomar on the 18th.

Overall: careful machinists who read what you send them, honest and conservative lead times, and no surcharge for getting parts into your hands. I have already told two other labs in our department to talk to them. If you are deciding who deserves to be on your preferred vendor list, put Arroyo Precision Works on it. Five stars, without reservation.

Ruben,

Fit test Monday was completely clean: all eight screws in with no forcing, flatness under 0.01 mm on the indicator, smooth baffle threads, no light leak in a 300 s dark frame with the lab lights on, and even anodizing with no bare spots. The adapter plate and baffle are exactly what we needed, and they are going to Palomar on the 18th.

I still owe you a thank you for three things: catching that bolt circle before you cut anything (that was my error, copied from an old drawing, and you saving the part saved our run), delivering to Robinson yourself on your way to Glendale at no charge, and turning the job around in nine days when the big vendor wanted six weeks.

I have written up the review on the CampusSource page and copied our purchasing office on it, so the shop gets the credit. I asked them to add you to the preferred vendor list. If anyone else in our department needs prototype or short-run aluminum work, I will point them your way.

Thanks again — I was genuinely happy about it.

Lin
